description.narrative: The most significant, expected project-level outcome is increased access to MSME and climate finance in Serbia. Beyond the project, IFC anticipates that the investment will promote greater market resilience by creating a strong benchmark for both EBS and other systemic banks to undertake issuances of MREL-eligible instruments and through demonstration effect and replication channel. SMEs dominate the Serbian business economy, accounting for 99% of all enterprises and employing more than 65% of the countrys labour force. Yet, according to the SME Finance Gap Report, the SME financing gap in Serbia is estimated at about 20% of GDP, with about 42% of SMEs being fully or partially credit-constrained. The long maturity SP MREL proceeds will allow the Bank to increase lending to MSMEs and to provide more longer-term investment loans. Also, IFC anticipates that this project will increase access to climate finance with minimum 30% use of proceeds dedicated to this area. Serbia faces a very large climate finance gap to meet its green transformation agenda and the Nationally Determined Contributions. With IFC financing, EBS is planning to increase its climate finance portfolio, which is focused on renewable energy, 3.6x times within 5 years from the current baseline.

The proposed project is to invest up to EUR65 million (equivalent to USD69 million) for IFCs own account in Minimum Requirement for Own Funds and Eligible Liabilities (MREL) eligible senior preferred (SP) instrument to be issued by Erste Bank A.D. Novi Sad (EBS or the Bank), a reputable bank in Serbia and a subsidiary of Erste Group, IFCs strategic partner and one of the largest banking groups in Europe (the Project). The proceeds of IFCs investment will be used to support the Banks MSME clients and climate change mitigant projects.
